title: The Test Loop: Typecheck, Unit Tests, and Contract Checks — Check

questions.prompt: What class of bug does `npm run typecheck` catch that unit tests might miss?
questions.explanation: Static typing flags structural mismatches (e.g., reading `result.moisture` when the field is `soilMoisture`) at compile time, across the whole codebase, without executing anything.
options: A renamed or mistyped field used across modules, caught statically before any code runs
A slow upstream API timing out
A redirect rule pointing to the wrong function

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a contract test in this system?
questions.explanation: Contract tests guard dev/prod parity by validating both producers against one shared schema, catching drift in CI rather than in the live UI.
options: To measure how fast the gateway responds
To assert that both the local mock and the production function honor the same response schema
To verify the LLM's answer quality

questions.prompt: Because the AI boundary is a deterministic mock, even end-to-end tests of the full path can run offline with stable expected results.
questions.explanation: True. Stubbing the only non-deterministic boundary keeps the entire compute path reproducible, so higher-level tests remain stable and require no network.

questions.prompt: Why run typecheck and unit tests on every save but heavier layers only before merge?
questions.explanation: A layered strategy puts the fastest, highest-yield checks in the inner loop and reserves slower, broader checks for the merge gate, keeping the dev loop fast without sacrificing coverage.
options: Because cheaper, faster layers catch the most bugs per second of runtime and fit a tight inner loop
Because Netlify limits how often you can run tests
Because contract tests don't matter in development
